functional relevance to GWI (secondary): mitochondrial/energy metabolism, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, cholinergic/detoxification pathways, HPA/stress axis, and aging/DNA repair.\n- In case of only; recurring themes included lipid/energy metabolism, peroxisomal fatty-acid oxidation, and neuroinflammation, but specific gene rankings diverged.\n\n## Cross-Chromosome Consensus GWI Themes\nThe strongest GWI candidates, balancing proximity and function, consistently fall into:\n- **Mitochondrial/energy metabolism:** Ppargc1a, Ucp2/Ucp3, Tomm40, Ndufc2, Bcl2l11, Mfn1, Slc16a9\n- **Lipid/energy metabolism:** Apoa1 cluster, Apoc1, Hmgcr, Npc1, Acaca, Scd1\n- **Neuroinflammation:** Tnf, H2/MHC, Stat3, Grn, Gfap, Cd200, Mertk\n- **HPA/steroid/stress axis:** Crhr1, Cyp17a1, Cyp21a\n- **Detoxification (organophosphate-relevant):** Cyp2c cluster, As3mt\n- **Aging/DNA repair:** Atm, Brca1, Recql4, Ercc1/2, Dnmt3a, Nnmt\n\n## Important Caveats (consistently raised across results)\n- Gene coordinate placements should be re-anchored to a single declared mouse assembly build (GRCm38/mm10 vs GRCm39/mm39) before distances are considered reliable. Several entries flagged with \"~near\" or \"?\" require verification.\n- Clustering was performed by visual/approximate windowing rather than a quantitative density threshold or LOD-support interval; clusters and rankings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.\n- Canonical GWI detoxification/cholinergic genes (Ache, Bche, Pon1, and CYP450 families) should be explicitly localized relative to the marker clusters, as they are the strongest established organophosphate-susceptibility candidates.\n- The very large merged blocks (e.g., Chr9 ~46\u2013106 Mb, Chr11 ~73\u2013106 Mb) likely contain multiple linked loci and should be subdivided into discrete sub-peaks for more reliable proximity-based ranking.'"
